spans.assertion: the paper's title states that hierarchical log-linear models show associations of no practical significance between red cards and players' skin tone

spans.note: author names, affiliation, correspondence email, blank lines

spans.assertion: no clear evidence of an association between players' skin tone and the number of red cards received in their career was found
nested log-linear models were compared to test the skin tone by red cards interaction
the skin tone by red cards interaction produced a very small increase in model fit (ΔG2(4)=10.63, p=.031, ORmax=1.016)
standardized parameters of the interaction were never significant (Zmax=1.859)
whether mean implicit bias (IAT) in referees' countries of origin moderates the skin tone/red card association was tested
nested model comparison found a significant improvement in model fit when adding the implicit-bias moderator
the direction of the moderation effect is not clearly interpretable in terms of racial bias
lower levels of implicit bias are related to more red cards among very-light-tone players
lower levels of implicit bias are related to fewer red cards among light-tone players
when present, associations are small enough in size to cast doubt on their practical significance
some groups of players with the same skin tone show lower or higher than expected proportions of red cards
overall, no clearly interpretable evidence of bias was found
a negative binomial mixed model with players as a random factor and skin tone as a fixed factor was first specified
estimation of the negative binomial mixed model failed
given the mixed-model failure, it was decided to estimate less computationally intensive models instead
a 3-way frequency table of red card counts by League (4 levels), Skintone (5 levels), and Matches (2 levels: with/without red card) was created
a log-linear model (League+Skintone terms) was specified and nested within a second model adding a Skintone*Redcards term, with the model comparison testing research question 1
a similar nested model-comparison procedure was followed for research questions 2a and 2b, using a 5-way frequency table with the two moderators dichotomized via median split
only players who were rated at the same skin-tone level by both raters were analyzed

spans.note: rationale for restricting to rater-agreed players: raters judged photos not real players, taken at differing times, yielding unclear judgments

spans.assertion: the percentage of perfect agreement between the two raters was less than 80%

spans.note: stated importance of using a highly reliable measure of the dependent variable

spans.assertion: nested models were compared using the difference in likelihood-ratio chi-square statistics
a conservative alpha of .01 was adopted given the very high number of observations
a significant interaction between Skintone, Matches, and IAT was found

spans.note: reports a reviewer comment criticizing dichotomization of moderators and dropping unrated players; not itself an analysis action

spans.assertion: log-linear models were their second choice because the mixed model's estimation procedure had failed
they believed there was no risk of low power, so restricting to perfect rater agreement increased the reliability of the independent variable without cost
no changes were made to the initial analytic approach in response to the reviewer comment
results show some association exists between players with similar skin tone and red cards
effect sizes are very small, casting doubt on the practical significance of the effects
the associations are not easily interpretable in terms of racial bias
no evidence was found that dark and very-dark-skinned players get the highest proportion of red cards

IAT moderates the skintone-redcard association such that referees from nations with higher implicit preference for light skin give fewer red cards to very-light-toned players and more to light-toned players, with categories 3-5 non-significant

lower explicit bias is associated with higher association between red cards and dark/very dark skin tone (categories 4,5)
